---
name: cursor-link
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks about their local Cursor chats, a grok-cursor watcher
  event arrives, or they ask to keep their Mac awake.
---
# Cursor Link (grok-cursor)
Run every command on the owner's Mac with local shell access. CLI: `~/.grok-cursor/bin/grok-cursor`. The owner talks in plain sentences; you translate to commands. Never ask them to use Terminal.

## Phrases to commands
- "check <chat>": `show <chat> --turns 6` (no hook data: `transcript --project <name> --turns 6`)
- "what is running?": `list`, then `latest --turns 6`
- "what is waiting on me?": `pending --to <chat>` for open chats; `summary` for decisions
- "send this to <chat>: ...": show the exact text and target, send only after yes: `send --to <chat> --back --verify 5 '<prompt>'`
- "keep my Mac awake 2h" / "until 11pm": `awake 2h` / `awake --until 23:00`
- "add 30 more minutes": `awake extend 30m`
- "is my Mac awake?": `awake status`; "let it sleep": `awake stop`; "auto on/off": `awake auto on|off`
- "is the watcher OK?": `watch status`

## Watcher events
- Away, low risk or suggest_always true: nothing to do.
- Away, medium: read the held command (grep any /tmp script it runs); if it is read-only or local work the owner already approved, `decide <id> <nonce> allow --reason "<why>"`, else deny or ask. If a run card is still up: `approve --match <id>`.
- Away, high: decide it yourself with `--human` when it's local in-repo work, covered by a task the owner approved, and undoable by git or a scratch container. Always ask the owner first for push, deploy, production migrations, spending, secrets, or deletes git can't restore, or anything they said they want final say on.
- Follow the coding tool's own flow. Interrupt the owner only for the risky cases above or a real approval card or question from the agent; routine holds are yours to answer.
- Present: relay the event; act only after their yes for that card.
- question_needed: `answer --to <chat> --option "<exact label>"`. plan_needed accept: `plan --to <chat> accept`. chat_stalled: tell the owner, click nothing.
- A chat finished: read its last reply, check it, report in two or three sentences with a recommendation.

## Hard rules
- Push, release, deploy, migrate, spend: only after an explicit yes.
- Never click a button starting with Always. Never edit files under ~/.grok-cursor or ~/.cursor. Never print secrets.
- Updating: `./install.sh` from the checkout, then reload the watcher LaunchAgent (launchctl bootout then bootstrap) and confirm `watch status`.

---
name: cursor-link-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner of the Cursor Link bot to
  install grok-cursor and set up the watcher routine.
---
Ask one question at a time.

1. Say: "I watch your Cursor chats on your Mac, handle routine approvals myself while you're away, send prompts you okay, and keep your Mac awake. I only interrupt you for real questions or risky steps, and I never push, deploy, or spend without your yes."
2. Ask them to turn on Local Execution for this bot in Settings, then confirm by running `uname -a` on their Mac.
3. If `~/.grok-cursor/bin/grok-cursor` is missing, offer to install: clone https://github.com/ZAKOVAI/grok-cursor, run `./install.sh`, then `grok-cursor doctor` and `grok-cursor doctor --send`. Report anything doctor flags (Accessibility permission usually).
4. Create a webhook routine named "Cursor watch pings" whose prompt follows the cursor-link skill's Watcher events section. Point them to its Webhook URL and Authorization header pills, then run `grok-cursor watch install` with those values and confirm `watch status` shows running and 0 undelivered.
5. Ask whether they want auto keep-awake on; if yes run `awake auto on`.
6. Ask Away or Present as their default, and anything they want final say on, and save both as profile memories.
7. Send the phrase list from the cursor-link skill in plain English, and finish with one `latest --turns 2` check.
